en: In the Milindapañha,
Chapter 8: The Questions and Answers of the Milindapañha,
the Elder said:
“Do you know, Great King, what time it is now?

“Yes, Bhante, I know: ‘The first watch has passed; the middle watch is underway; the torches are being lit; the four banners have been ordered out—they shall depart from the royal treasury as gifts for the king.
The Yonakas said, “Well done, Great King! Wise is the Elder.”
“Yes, indeed, sir; the Elder is wise. Such a teacher and a disciple like me—before long, the wise one will understand the Dhamma.
Satisfied by his answer to the question, the king covered the Elder Nāgasena with a blanket worth a hundred thousand pieces of gold and said:
“Venerable Nāgasena, from this day forward, I provide you with a meal for eight hundred people; whatever [is required]...”
“It is allowable in the inner palace, and with that I invite you,” he said.
“Enough, Great King; I live on it.
“I know, venerable Nāgasena, that you live; nevertheless, protect yourself and protect me as well.”
“How do you protect yourself? You must protect yourself thus: ‘May no slander come to me, saying, “Nāgasena does not please King Milinda, nor has he gained anything at all.
How do you protect me? You must protect me thus: ‘May no slander come to me, saying, “King Milinda, though pleased, does not show his pleasure.
“So be it, Great King,” [he replied].
“Venerable sir, just as the lion, the king of beasts, even when cast into a golden cage, remains with his face turned outward;
even so, venerable sir, although I dwell at home, I remain with my face turned outward.
If I were to go forth from the home life into homelessness, venerable sir, I would not live long, for I have many enemies.”
Then the Venerable Nāgasena, having answered King Milinda’s question, rose from his seat and went to the monastery.
Not long after the Venerable Nāgasena had departed, this thought occurred to King Milinda:
"What did I ask, and what was answered by the venerable Nāgasena?"
Then it occurred to King Milinda:
"Everything has been well questioned by me, and everything has been well answered by the Venerable Nāgasena.
And it occurred to the Venerable Nāgasena when he had gone to the monastery:
“What was asked by King Milinda? What was answered by me?
Then it occurred to the Venerable Nāgasena:
“Everything was well asked by King Milinda; everything was well answered by me.”
Then, when that night had passed, the Venerable Nāgasena dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe, and went to the residence of King Milinda. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Then King Milinda, having paid homage to the Venerable Nāgasena, sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, King Milinda said this to the Venerable Nāgasena:
“Venerable sir, you should not think, ‘Nāgasena was asked a question by me,’ and spend the remainder of that night with only that joy.
Rather, Venerable sir, during that remainder of the night, this thought occurred to me:
‘What have I asked? What has the venerable one answered? [And I realized: ‘Everything I asked was well-asked; everything the venerable one answered was well-answered.’”
The Elder also spoke thus:
“Great King, you should not think, ‘I have answered the questions of King Milinda,’ and spend the remainder of that night with such joy alone.
For it was this thought, Great King, that occurred to me during the remainder of that night:”

"What was asked by King Milinda? What was answered by me? "Everything was well asked by King Milinda; everything was well answered by me. Thus those great Nāgas rejoiced in one another's well-spoken words.
The Questions and Answers of the *Milindapañha* are concluded.
